name: Stavkirker (Stave Churches of Norway and replicas/heritage diaspora)
title: Stavkirker (Stave Churches of Norway and replicas/heritage diaspora)
description: Comprehensive catalog of stave churches (stavkirker) — Norway's UNESCO-listed medieval wooden church heritage. Includes the 28 surviving original stave churches (Urnes — UNESCO World Heritage Site 1979 Q210678 Luster, Borgund Q755010 Lærdal, Heddal Q1129816 Notodden — Norway's largest, Hopperstad Vik, Lom Q1170070, Gol Q1107502 now at Norsk Folkemuseum Oslo, Kaupanger, Kvernes, Reinli, Ringebu, Rødven, Røldal, Torpo, Tønjum, Undredal, Uvdal, Vang, Øye and others), plus the historic stave churches in the demolished/lost category (Revne stavkirker i Norge — 77 documented lost stave churches including Atrå, Eggedal, Flå, Hemsedal, Hjartdal, Lillehammer, Mæl, Sauland, Tuddal, Vegusdal and many more), plus modern reconstructions and copies (Kopier av stavkirker — including Fantoft (rebuilt after 1992 arson), Gol nye, Heimaey Iceland Norwegian-style copies, Gustav Adolf Sweden copy, Vang stavkirke now in Karpacz Poland, etc.). Compiled via Norwegian Wikipedia category traversal (Kategori:Stavkirker + Kategori:Revne stavkirker + Kategori:Revne stavkirker i Norge + Kategori:Kopier av stavkirker) cross-referenced with Wikidata. Each record includes multilingual names (Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, English, Danish, Swedish, German, French, Dutch, Icelandic, Finnish where available), administrative location (kommune), coordinates, year built, year dissolved where applicable, Commons image URL, Riksantikvaren heritage register ID (askeladden/kulturminne), construction materials, religious denomination, heritage designation status, and Wikipedia sitelinks across 10 languages.
